brokerStatements.deleteHint: Dividend tax will again be counted without crediting what was withheld abroad, and cost will no longer come from the statement.
brokerStatements.title: Broker statement (P&L)
brokerStatements.hint: Revolut → brokerage account → Documents → profit and loss statement (PDF). It gives the tax withheld from dividends abroad (it reduces the Polish one), the cost of shares without a purchase in the journal (for example after a spin-off) and Revolut’s gain for checking. Transactions are still imported from CSV.
brokerStatements.unmatched: the rest found no transaction in the journal — import the CSV for the same period

losses.title: Past years’ losses
losses.hint: Yours, not an account’s: one entry per year for all brokers.
losses.deleteHint: The loss of {year} will no longer reduce the tax.

dividends.title: Dividends

ledger.reverseHint: The original stays in the journal, and the reversal cancels its effect on positions, cash and taxes.

ledger.emptyHint: Transactions appear when you mark actions in a report, import positions.json or record a trade by hand.

kind.RiskReview: sale only on an exit signal

mode.UpdateHint: Like “Append”, and rows imported earlier with other figures are overwritten from the statement (reversal + a new record).
mode.FromScratchHint: The whole account journal is reversed, then the statement is imported. Use it if you start the bookkeeping over.

importPositions.noPositions: The file has no positions array

importPositions.hint: A Python flow file: the positions become journal transactions (a contribution for the whole value and buys at the entry price). Importing again duplicates nothing.

addSub.title: New sub-portfolio

plan.splitHow: How to split the contribution between sub-portfolios
plan.splitHint: “To the one lagging” keeps the shares without selling; “By shares” is always the same.
plan.minTradeHint: Smaller buys are skipped, the money is parked
plan.trimBandHint: A position in profit is sold down to its target only when it exceeds the target by more than this many percent of the portfolio
plan.driftBandHint: A larger drift — the report suggests an internal transfer between sub-portfolios
plan.fractional: Fractional shares (the broker allows buying part of an ETF)

review.whatNext: What happens next: at this time a

review.changeLater: If you want to change something later
review.changeShares: Shares, strategies, adding or retiring a part
review.changeSharesWhere: — the account page, the “Sub-portfolios” block (Settings → Accounts).

reports.hint: — a list of actions for the broker: how much to contribute, what to buy and sell. The strategy sets which reports exist, and it has its own time. But when a report arrives is up to you: for example, if your salary comes on the 10th, put the rebalance on the 10th — the money will already be on the account. You can change it any time in the “Report schedule” block on the account page (
reports.noScheduled: The chosen strategies make no scheduled reports — they can be generated by hand.

done.title: The account is ready
done.haveInvestmentsHint: Upload a Revolut statement (CSV) — the transaction history, positions and cash appear automatically.
done.fromScratchHint: Generate the first report: how much to contribute and which ETFs to buy.
done.viewAccountHint: Shares, strategies, report schedule — everything can be changed later.

contributions.hint: — how much you plan to add regularly. In every report the service says how much to contribute and what to buy with that money. The amount can be changed with every report.

sleeves.strategyHint: decides each time which ETFs to hold in the sub-portfolio.
sleeves.changeLater: Shares and strategies can be changed later, and parts added or retired, on the account page (
sleeves.simpleHint: One sub-portfolio, one strategy. Best to start with.
sleeves.europeUsHint: Two parts with different sets of ETFs — more diversification.
sleeves.customHint: Any number of parts and strategies.

account.accountHint: — your real brokerage account (for example at Revolut). The service does not connect to the broker: it works out the plan, and you carry it out in the broker’s app and mark it here (or upload a statement).
account.name: What to call it
account.currencyHint: The plan, cash and value are counted in it. ETFs in other currencies are converted at the official rate. Amounts can be shown in any currency (the switch at the top).
